title: Neural networks and fuzzy logic
lead: A guided route through neural network learning methods and fuzzy reasoning.

title: Neurons, activations and network foundations
lead: See how weighted signals, bias, activation, architecture, and learning fit together before working through the course’s training procedures.

title: Threshold logic and perceptron learning
lead: How fixed thresholds implement logic, and how a perceptron learns a linear decision boundary.

title: ADALINE and MADALINE learning
lead: How ADALINE learns from linear error and how early MADALINE rules choose hidden-unit updates.

title: Widrow-Hoff derivation and LMS calculations
lead: Derive the no-half Widrow–Hoff objective, connect its quadratic geometry to LMS, and work the source vectors through two complete epochs.

title: Multilayer networks and backpropagation
lead: Follow an MLP from a forward prediction through chain-rule deltas to simultaneous weight updates, with the lecture’s examples and a checked two-epoch teaching trace.

title: Backpropagation variations and deeper networks
lead: Compare update history, batch corrections, adaptive rates, activation gains, and a full two-hidden-layer backpropagation pass.

title: Probabilistic neural networks
lead: A memory-based classifier that turns stored examples into Gaussian class-density estimates.

title: Crisp and fuzzy sets
lead: A source-faithful introduction to crisp and fuzzy membership, notation, and the standard set operations.

title: Relations and matrix composition
lead: A calculation-first guide to ordered-pair relations, matrix composition, tolerance closure, and relation strengths.

title: Membership, fuzzification and defuzzification
lead: Read membership-function shapes, fuzzify crisp inputs, form weak cuts, and compare six scalar defuzzification methods with complete calculations.

title: Classical logic and crisp rule relations
lead: A guided route from binary propositions and proof patterns to crisp IF/ELSE relations and inference.

title: Fuzzy propositions, linguistic variables and implications
lead: How graded propositions, implication relations, linguistic variables and hedges connect fuzzy words to rule reasoning.

title: Mamdani, Sugeno, Tsukamoto and ANFIS
lead: Trace canonical rule evaluation, compare Mamdani, TSK, and Tsukamoto inference, and see how ANFIS layers connect TSK with hybrid learning.
